sources.note: Political institutions, mid-seventeenth-century wars, serf labor and religious divisions. Interpretive claims about national character are not repeated.

sources.note: Map and historical commentary on three partitions, reform, the 1794 uprising and loss of sovereignty in 1795.

sources.title: Central Archives of Historical Records: The Constitution of 3 May 1791
sources.note: 2018 publication with historical introduction, surviving-document discussion and a contemporary English translation; especially pp. 31-33 and Articles IV-VI.

sources.title: Polish History Museum: Commission of National Education, 1773
sources.note: Commission established 14 October, proclamation 24 October 1773; curriculum, teacher training and Society for Elementary Books.

sources.title: Wilanow Museum: Discover the Royal Residence
sources.note: Construction from 1677, royal apartments, gardens, family and learned patronage; later owners and additions distinguished.

sources.title: Radoslaw Grzeskowiak: Visiting the bed of Queen Mary
sources.note: Museum study of letters and diaries: Maria Kazimiera adopting French bedside reception customs in 1662 and continuing them later.

sources.title: Maciej Jasinski: Johannes Hevelius
sources.note: Museum account of 1647 lunar study, 1673 instruments and engravings, Elisabeth Koopmann Hevelius and publications of 1690.

sources.title: Magdalena Gorska: Astronomy and politics in Wilanow Palace decoration
sources.note: Facade inscription REFULSIT SOL IN CLYPEIS, biblical reference and interpretation of shields, sun and royal authority.

sources.title: POLIN Museum: The Gwozdziec synagogue
sources.note: Wooden building attributed to around 1640, painted interior, women’s rooms and later school annex; sources differ on precise construction and destruction dates.

sources.title: POLIN Museum: Core exhibition
sources.note: Jewish Town gallery 1648-1772: markets, homes and religious life; Encounters with Modernity explains changed jurisdictions after partition.

sources.title: POLIN Museum: One Hour, Eight Highlights
sources.note: Gallery 4: painted ceiling renovation in 1729 and 2011-2012 reconstruction with traditional materials and tools. Construction/destruction dates differ from another museum page and are not used as exact dates.

sources.title: Wojciech Bis: Baths and bathrooms in the seventeenth century
sources.note: Museum research article based on 2007 archaeological study; Kazanowski palace bath, urban baths and social/medical services.

sources.title: Anna Penkala-Jastrzebska: Objects of noble personal hygiene
sources.note: 2020 study of seventeenth- and eighteenth-century household inventories: basins, combs, wigs and chamber pots. Illustrated nineteenth-century toothbrush is outside this card’s period.

sources.title: Archaeological Museum in Gdansk: Latrines
sources.note: Agnieszka Ruta: late-medieval and early-modern urban sanitation, timber linings, backfills and limits of superstructure reconstruction.

sources.title: Archaeological Museum in Gdansk: Pharmacies in old Gdansk
sources.note: Adam Szarszewski and Piotr Paluchowski, Medical University of Gdansk: pharmacies, supervision and the 1665 Dispensatorium Gedanense.

proposedOverrides.name: Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
proposedOverrides.summary: The Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth combined elected monarchy with powerful noble institutions. Its communities produced astronomical books, decorated buildings and educational reforms, alongside everyday trades and household work. These map dates show only part of its history, which began in 1569 and ended politically in 1795.

proposedOverrides.name: Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
proposedOverrides.summary: The remaining Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth pursued education and constitutional reform after the first partition. Russia, Prussia and Austria ultimately divided its territory; independent government ended in 1795. This map interval shows only its final years.

entities.geometryStatus: Imported coordinates unchanged and unverified. The 1783 Poland feature display interval is clipped at 1795, also preserved by the importer SPLITS rule; intermediate partition boundaries remain unverified.

identityEvidence.assessment: Imported Poland label and location identify the surviving Commonwealth after 1772. Endpoint corrected from 1800 to historical dissolution in 1795. Exact partition boundaries remain unverified; 1783 is map coverage, not a foundation.
